title: Prediction residuals in spatial transcriptomics reveal microenvironmental heterogeneity in cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Prediction residuals in spatial transcriptomics reveal microenvironmental heterogeneity in cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Prediction residuals in spatial transcriptomics reveal microenvironmental heterogeneity in cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients.

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients.

evidence.text: The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients.
In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Prediction residuals in spatial transcriptomics reveal microenvironmental heterogeneity in cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors.

【Abstract · abstract-1-8】Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathway profiles were more similar within patients, although the permutation test allowed only nine assignments (p=1/9).

evidence.text: Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors.

Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathway profiles were more similar within patients, although the permutation test allowed only nine assignments (p=1/9).
